analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: SOGGY START (U.S. Equities Color, 16 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed sharply lower on Monday 16 Nov: S&P -192bps at 7,416 with a $5.3bn market-on-close imbalance to buy, NDX -267bps, R2K -175bps, Dow -141bps. VIX rose 1979bps to 23.12. Volume was 17.916bn shares against a year-to-date daily average of 18.555bn.

Global Tech and AI led the decline (NVDA -4.5%, DRAM -6%, SMH -5%, Neoclouds -7%). The desk says the market is still absorbing Jensen Huang's departure from NVDA and what it means for the wider AI ecosystem.
Reports that Congress is moving to pass tighter AI chip export rules added to the pressure on tech this morning. An FT report separately says Huang is eyeing a possible return to NVDA.
The desk rated overall floor activity a 4 on a 1-10 scale. Asset manager and hedge fund flows were muted ahead of a busy week.
Staples saw a flight to safety. The desk attributes part of it to reversion after heavier short supply across nearly all subsectors last week, per GS Prime Brokerage.

Single-stock movers were mostly attributed to Monday data reads and sell-side commentary: TSCO +4%, BBWI -9%, VSXY -5%. ARMK rose 1% on EPS after starting in the red and being quickly defended, with longer positioning already coming in.
Next on the earnings and events calendar: the NKE investor day tomorrow, and earnings from AS, VIK and HD.

Derivatives desk: index options are expensive across the board after an aggressive bid in vol, while conviction remained very low. The S&P realized its entire weekly implied move in one session, with QQQ and IWM close behind, and both vol and skew jumped.
Overall option volumes were muted, following a week of light positioning and a pickup in ETF short interest.
Single-stock option flow: the desk saw buying of capped upside (call structures with a cap) in AMZN, MU and TSM, and longer-dated outright downside protection in semis.
NVDA is the focus tomorrow, with a 7.8% implied 1-day move. The S&P straddle for the rest of the week prices 2%, which the desk says still looks underpriced given the current market regime.

sector_views.rationale: Desk describes a flight to safety into Staples, helped by reversion after heavy short supply across nearly all subsectors last week per GS PB. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: ARMK +1% on its EPS print (no figures given). The report says the stock started in red and was quickly defended, with longer positioning already coming in.
Upcoming: NKE investor day tomorrow (17 Nov), and earnings from AS, VIK and HD. No estimates given.
NVDA carries a 7.8% implied 1-day move for tomorrow, per the derivatives desk. The report does not state the event behind it.
crypto_views: Bitcoin was -6bps at $64,959 in the closing market summary. No further crypto commentary.
